name: Mario Vargas Llosa
role: Peruvian-Spanish novelist, liberal political essayist and presidential candidate (1990)
summary: Vargas Llosa moved from revolutionary socialism to democratic liberalism, defending markets, civil liberties and constitutional restraints. His mature views combined social liberalism and open migration with opposition to authoritarian government and qualified support for intervention against tyranny.

abortion-legal.rationale: He supports a woman’s choice during the first three months of pregnancy.

allow-dual-citizenship.rationale: He holds Spanish nationality alongside his Peruvian one and says he has never felt any incompatibility between them.

assisted-dying.rationale: He defends a lucid person’s right to choose an end to unbearable suffering.

central-planning.rationale: He attributes communist economic failure to collectivist and statist institutions.

corporate-influence.rationale: He condemns United Fruit’s manipulation of American policy to overthrow Guatemala’s elected government.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: He defends judicial independence and legal accountability despite a politician’s electoral position.

death-penalty.rationale: He unequivocally rejects executions, including for especially cruel crimes, because errors cannot be corrected.

democracy-best.rationale: He explicitly prefers even highly imperfect democracies to supposedly perfect dictatorships.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: He calls overlapping cultures a major social strength rather than a national weakness.

economic-freedom.rationale: He explicitly treats economic and political freedom as inseparable.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: He argues that isolation and self-sufficiency preserve poverty rather than living cultures.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He tentatively considers UN-imposed peace backed by major powers.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He celebrates Latin America’s mixed ancestry and rejects ethnically exclusive accounts of national identity.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: He demands that political leaders confront nuclear escalation and possible human extinction.

free-trade.rationale: He defends globally interconnected markets as opportunities for material and cultural progress.

gradual-change.rationale: He abandoned armed revolutionary change for gradual reform through democratic institutions.

harm-principle.rationale: He defends organizing one’s life by personal values without damaging other people’s lives.

immigration-favours-shared-culture.rationale: He argues for open borders 'pure and simple', where anyone may settle if they obey the law, and says immigrants are always a factor of progress; he proposes no selection by culture.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: He praises pension privatization and criticizes opposition to privatizing American Social Security.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: He says science and industry have made human life far better than primitive existence.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: He rejects reducing Ukraine to Russian vassalage or denying its freedom to choose alliances.

land-redistribution.rationale: He praises Árbenz’s distribution of idle land to Guatemalan peasants.

legalize-drugs.rationale: He advocates allowing adult drug use, replacing repression with information and treatment.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He calls markets the most effective wealth-producing mechanism, while rejecting market fundamentalism.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: He explicitly rejects the economy as history’s principal driver, emphasizing ideas and culture.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He supports public social services and high-quality public schooling beyond law enforcement and defense.

one-party-rule.rationale: In his memoir he describes Mexico's PRI as a party dictatorship that keeps up democratic appearances by tolerating elections and a critical press.

open-borders.rationale: He explicitly calls for immigration without borders, while emphasizing integration and opportunity.

person-over-state.rationale: His liberalism gives individual interests priority over the state and defends personal autonomy.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He explicitly praises European unity and Macron’s support for the European Union.

population-transfer.rationale: He condemns Palestinian forced displacement and threatened expulsion as part of collective punishment.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He opposes bureaucratic protection of a fixed national identity against cultural exchange.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: He says democratic countries should pursue an energetic policy of incentives and sanctions to further democratization in poor countries, including tying aid to the private sector.

property-fundamental.rationale: He argued that political freedom and representative democracy are inseparable from respect for private property, and led the campaign against nationalising the banks.

public-ownership.rationale: He opposed bank nationalization and later criticized renewed nationalizations in Argentina.

purge-loanwords.rationale: He criticizes French penalties on English loanwords as nationalist cultural protection.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: In his 1996 column he calls anti-immigration policies a cover for xenophobia and racism, rejects fear of black, mulatto, yellow or copper-skinned immigrants, and backs open borders.

reduce-immigration.rationale: He urges Europe to welcome immigrants as indispensable contributors to prosperity.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: He supports lawful presidential removal if corruption allegations against Kuczynski are proved.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: He rejects authoritarian governments claiming repression is necessary for free-market development.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He argues that liberal policy must adapt to reality rather than follow fixed ideological recipes.

return-to-foraging.rationale: He rejects a proposed return to primitive natural living as another doomed utopia.

right-to-secede.rationale: He opposes Catalan independence and defends Spain’s common democratic constitutional order.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: He explicitly supports legal same-sex marriage as a necessary reform.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: He defended Fujimori's conviction and his remarks on the later pardon qualify that, so the evidence is only partly one way.

separate-church-state.rationale: He explicitly advocates separation of religious and state authority.

separated-powers.rationale: He insists unavoidable governing power must be counterbalanced and checked.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He praises independent judges prosecuting powerful politicians and supports sanctions against a corrupt president.

state-harmful.rationale: He rejects anarchist abolition of power while insisting government be constrained.

strong-leader.rationale: He condemned Fujimori's closing of Congress and argued that a state of law with an elected congress and independent judiciary must restrain those in power.

suppress-opposition.rationale: His mature political outlook rejects the persecution of dissidents under communist and military dictatorships.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He condemns Putin’s attempt to recreate imperial control through the invasion of Ukraine.

turn-back-illegal-migrants.rationale: He calls police measures to seal borders and expel illegal immigrants useless and corrosive of democracy, and cites the drugging of African migrants for expulsion in Spain as a disgrace.

widespread-small-property.rationale: He approves making those peasants private entrepreneurs protected from renewed landlord domination.

notes: Updated people prompt reread before completion. Full Lindau lecture, globalization essay and accessible interviews were downloaded and theme-searched; the Nobel website returned403, so no inaccessible Nobel text is cited. Career coverage includes his early revolutionary commitment,1990 campaign and later writings through2023. Later clear positions supersede youthful views. Candidate endorsements do not establish agreement with those candidates’ policies. Fujimori accountability is qualified by the later pardon report. Environmental evidence supports conservation with industry, not climate-policy details; technological warnings about misinformation do not establish particular AI, encryption or automation policies. All ten themes and every remaining null were reviewed against the evidence. No positions were inferred from labels, fictional characters or associates; no inferred answers. His1983 Uchuraccay commission blamed villagers; later archival research disputes its handling of military evidence. That controversy is acknowledged without attributing critics’ claims about his motives as his own positions. 2026-11-20 pass (claude-sonnet-5-5): read his non-fiction in the local library (Language of Passion, Making Waves, A Fish in the Water, In Praise of Reading and Fiction) for immigration, democracy promotion, property, leadership, nationality, violence, trade, prices and international justice; Touchstones, Temptation of the Impossible and A Writer's Reality searched by keyword. Most remaining statements are about topics he never took a position on.
